findings.title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next resource bundle
findings.body: This bundle is consumed by the account console through i18next, where placeholders must be written as `{{0}}` (see every other entry in this file, e.g. `error-username-invalid-character='{{0}}' contains invalid character.`). The key was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. i18next does not interpolate single braces and has no support for MessageFormat `choice`, so the user will now see the raw text including `{0}` and `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` whenever a multivalued attribute fails size validation. The Java MessageFormat form is only correct for the server-side `themes/src/main/resources/theme/base/**` bundles.

findings.title: Java MessageFormat/choice syntax used in an i18next resource bundle
findings.body: Same problem as in the account-ui bundle: this file is loaded by the admin console via i18next, which interpolates `{{n}}` and does not understand MessageFormat `choice`. Replacing `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` with `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.` makes the message render literally (placeholders and the choice expression visible to the admin) instead of being substituted.

findings.title: Diff computation can throw StringIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of reporting the problem
findings.body:
The common-prefix length (`start`) and common-suffix length (`end`) are computed independently, so for strings that differ by a repeated substring they can overlap and `start > length - end`. Example: value `

x

` sanitizes to `

x

`; the prefix loop yields start=3 and the suffix loop yields end=8, so `sanitized.substring(3, 8 - 8)` = `substring(3, 0)` throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The Maven plugin then fails with an opaque runtime exception rather than emitting the intended "Illegal HTML in key ..." message. Clamp the indices (e.g. `end = Math.min(end, Math.min(value.length(), sanitized.length()) - start)`).

findings.title: Missing English counterpart aborts the build with a bare RuntimeException
findings.body: `verifySafeHtml()` derives the English bundle path by string replacement and then opens it unconditionally; if the file does not exist (community-only theme/message directory with no `messages_en.properties` under `resources`, a bundle without a locale suffix where the regex does not match, or a newly added community locale) a `FileNotFoundException` is wrapped into a plain `RuntimeException`. The surrounding `verify()` already declares `MojoExecutionException` and wraps IO errors of the main file properly, so this path produces an inconsistent, hard build failure with no actionable message. Either skip the HTML check (or report a verification message) when the English bundle is absent, and throw `MojoExecutionException` otherwise.

findings.title: Anchor verification is order-sensitive and mutates the string it is iterating
findings.body: `santizeAnchors` pairs the n-th anchor tag of the translation with the n-th anchor tag of the English source and requires exact equality. A translation that legitimately reorders two links (English `... .. ... ..`, translation with the links swapped) is reported as "Didn't find anchor tag" even though it contains exactly the same tags, i.e. a false build failure. In addition, `value` is reassigned inside the loop while `matcher` keeps iterating the original snapshot, and the removal is done with `replaceFirst` on the *English* group, so the occurrence that is removed is not necessarily the one just matched. Compare the multiset of anchor tags instead of their positions.

findings.title: Anchor failure message does not say which key or file is affected
findings.body: The message added here is only "Didn't find anchor tag <a ...> in original string", while all other messages produced by this class include the key and the file name. With hundreds of message bundles being verified, a build failure with this text gives the contributor no way to locate the offending entry. Include `key` (already passed into the method but unused) and `file`.

findings.title: Properties are read as ISO-8859-1 while Keycloak theme bundles are UTF-8
findings.body: `new PropertyResourceBundle(InputStream)` is specified to decode the stream as ISO-8859-1. The theme bundles checked here (Arabic, Chinese, Greek, Ukrainian, ...) are stored as UTF-8, and the server reads them as UTF-8, so every non-ASCII value is mojibake inside the verifier. The consequence is that the "Illegal HTML in key ... : '<x>' vs '<y>'" diagnostics printed for those locales are garbled and hard to act on, and any future check that depends on the real characters would be wrong. Use `new PropertyResourceBundle(new InputStreamReader(fis, StandardCharsets.UTF_8))` (same for the English bundle) to match how the files are actually encoded.

findings.title: Purely cosmetic serialization differences are reported as "Illegal HTML"
findings.body:
The check compares the translation byte-for-byte with the sanitizer's re-serialized output, so differences that are not security relevant (the sanitizer emits `
`, so every `
` in a bundle fails; likewise attribute quoting/order or added whitespace) are reported with the message "Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...". This is why ~20 unrelated locale files in this PR had to be rewritten from `
` to `
`, and future contributors will get a misleading "Illegal HTML" error for valid markup. Either normalize both sides before comparing, or reword the message so it distinguishes "tag not allowed" from "formatting differs from canonical form".

findings.title: containsHtml only detects lower-case tag names
findings.body:
`HTML_TAGS = Pattern.compile("<[a-z]+[^>]*>")` is case sensitive, so an English source value written with upper/mixed case markup (e.g. `
` or ``) is classified as containing no HTML. The translation is then validated with POLICY_NO_HTML and every tag it contains is reported as illegal, producing a false failure. Compile the pattern with `CASE_INSENSITIVE`.

findings.title: No test asserts that a valid bundle produces no findings
findings.body:
All four tests only assert `hasItem(...)` on the returned list, so nothing verifies the absence of false positives: there is no fixture where a translation legitimately keeps the HTML of an English source that contains HTML (e.g. ``/`
`/an unchanged ``), nor a case with MessageFormat `choice` or `{{...}}` placeholders, and no assertion that `verify()` returns an empty list for such a file. Given that the new sanitizer compares the exact serialized form, a regression that starts flagging every valid bundle would not be caught by this suite. Also note the assertions were relaxed from `Matchers.contains` to `Matchers.hasItem`, so additional unexpected messages are now silently accepted.

findings.title: Lithuanian bundle now contains Italian text
findings.body: `totpStep1` was replaced with `Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:` which is Italian, not Lithuanian. Lithuanian users of the account console will see an Italian sentence on the OTP setup page. The same wrong-language string was introduced in `themes/src/main/resources-community/theme/base/login/messages/messages_lt.properties` (`loginTotpStep1`). If the old value had to be changed because it contained links, it should be translated to Lithuanian (or left to the translators) rather than copied from the Italian bundle.

findings.title: Traditional Chinese text added to the Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) bundle
findings.body: `totpStep1=在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：` uses Traditional Chinese characters and Taiwanese terminology (手機/應用程式) and appears to be copied from the zh_TW bundle. In a zh_CN bundle it should read something like `在您的手机上安装以下应用程序之一：`; as it stands, Simplified Chinese users get a Traditional Chinese sentence.
